market_context: U.S. equities are narrowly mixed and leadership remains concentrated in a rebound in AI-linked mega-cap technology: AP reported that Nvidia and other large tech shares offset Apple’s decline, while more S&P 500 constituents were falling than rising. (apnews.com) Apple’s post-earnings weakness is tied to softer gross-margin expectations amid memory-cost pressure, while election-day uncertainty and the recent AI-spending/valuation selloff argue for a cautious afternoon rather than broad risk-on follow-through. (investing.com)

predictions.reasoning: SPY has already retreated from its $756.50 intraday high to $754.83, while the Dow remains negative and AP reported that declining S&P 500 members outnumbered advancers despite the index’s gain. ([apnews.com) With the advance concentrated in a small group of AI names and election-related uncertainty still present, a modest late-session fade is more likely than a sustained breakout.

QQQ is off its $688.69 session high even as the largest AI beneficiaries lead, signaling that the early technology rebound has already begun to lose momentum. The Nasdaq entered this week after a sharp October pullback driven by concerns that AI infrastructure spending is outrunning near-term cash generation. (fidelity.com)

Apple remains the clearest stock-specific negative catalyst: despite beating on quarterly profit and revenue, investors focused on pressure from memory costs and lower gross-margin guidance. (apnews.com) Its price is also below the opening-area high of $334.50, suggesting rallies are being sold rather than building a recovery.

MSFT is trading essentially at its $518.54 intraday high after a 2.23% advance, leaving limited room for additional upside if the broader tech rebound continues to fade. Broader investor concern remains focused on the scale of hyperscaler AI financing and capital spending, a backdrop that increases the odds of afternoon profit-taking in a leader already near its high. (axios.com)
